answer: Rotating seed auction. Each epoch a verifiable random seed selects a small committee from all registered agents, and only committee members may create new identities until the next seed, which no one can precompute. An attacker must hold many agents through an umber of prior epochs hoping to land seats, and each failed attempt costs the full registration effort at the orchard of identities they built. At the nadir of their odds, expected cost per successful sybil scales with committee size times epoch length, making sustained infiltration economically ruinous.
